ESV.1: The LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did to Sarah as he had promised.
ESV.2: And Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age at the time of which God had spoken to him.
ESV.3: Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore him, Isaac.
ESV.4: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
ESV.5: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
ESV.6: And Sarah said, “God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh over me.”
ESV.7: And she said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”
ESV.8: And the child grew and was weaned. And Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.
ESV.9: But Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.
ESV.10: So she said to Abraham, “Cast out this slave woman with her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac.”
ESV.11: And the thing was very displeasing to Abraham on account of his son.
ESV.12: But God said to Abraham, “Be not displeased because of the boy and because of your slave woman. Whatever Sarah says to you, do as she tells you, for through Isaac shall your offspring be named.
ESV.13: And I will make a nation of the son of the slave woman also, because he is your offspring.”
ESV.14: So Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, along with the child, and sent her away. And she departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
ESV.15: When the water in the skin was gone, she put the child under one of the bushes.
ESV.16: Then she went and sat down opposite him a good way off, about the distance of a bowshot, for she said, “Let me not look on the death of the child.” And as she sat opposite him, she lifted up her voice and wept.
ESV.17: And God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, “What troubles you, Hagar? Fear not, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
ESV.18: Up! Lift up the boy, and hold him fast with your hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”
ESV.19: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
ESV.20: And God was with the boy, and he grew up. He lived in the wilderness and became an expert with the bow.
ESV.21: He lived in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
ESV.22: At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham, “God is with you in all that you do.
ESV.23: Now therefore swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my descendants or with my posterity, but as I have dealt kindly with you, so you will deal with me and with the land where you have sojourned.”
ESV.25: When Abraham reproved Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized,
ESV.26: Abimelech said, “I do not know who has done this thing; you did not tell me, and I have not heard of it until today.”
ESV.27: So Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant.
ESV.28: Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock apart.
ESV.29: And Abimelech said to Abraham, “What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs that you have set apart?”
ESV.30: He said, “These seven ewe lambs you will take from my hand, that this  may be a witness for me that I dug this well.”
ESV.31: Therefore that place was called Beersheba,  because there both of them swore an oath.
ESV.32: So they made a covenant at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army rose up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
ESV.33: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and called there on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
ESV.34: And Abraham sojourned many days in the land of the Philistines.

NKJV.1: And the LORD visited Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah as He had spoken.
NKJV.2: For Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
NKJV.3: And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him—whom Sarah bore to him— Isaac.
NKJV.4: Then Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
NKJV.5: Now Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
NKJV.6: And Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and all who hear will laugh with me.”
NKJV.7: She also said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”
NKJV.8: So the child grew and was weaned. And Abraham made a great feast on the same day that Isaac was weaned.
NKJV.9: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, scoffing.
NKJV.10: Therefore she said to Abraham, “Cast out this bondwoman and her son; for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, namely with Isaac.”
NKJV.11: And the matter was very displeasing in Abraham’s sight because of his son.
NKJV.12: But God said to Abraham, “Do not let it be displeasing in your sight because of the lad or because of your bondwoman. Whatever Sarah has said to you, listen to her voice; for in Isaac your seed shall be called.
NKJV.13: Yet I will also make a nation of the son of the bondwoman, because he is your seed.”
NKJV.14: So Abraham rose early in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water; and putting it on her shoulder, he gave it and the boy to Hagar, and sent her away. Then she departed and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.
NKJV.15: And the water in the skin was used up, and she placed the boy under one of the shrubs.
NKJV.16: Then she went and sat down across from him at a distance of about a bowshot; for she said to herself, “Let me not see the death of the boy.” So she sat opposite him, and lifted her voice and wept.
NKJV.17: And God heard the voice of the lad. Then the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said to her, “What ails you, Hagar? Fear not, for God has heard the voice of the lad where he is.
NKJV.18: Arise, lift up the lad and hold him with your hand, for I will make him a great nation.”
NKJV.19: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled the skin with water, and gave the lad a drink.
NKJV.20: So God was with the lad; and he grew and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer.
NKJV.21: He dwelt in the Wilderness of Paran; and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
NKJV.22: And it came to pass at that time that Abimelech and Phichol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham, saying, “God is with you in all that you do.
NKJV.23: Now therefore, swear to me by God that you will not deal falsely with me, with my offspring, or with my posterity; but that according to the kindness that I have done to you, you will do to me and to the land in which you have dwelt.”
NKJV.25: Then Abraham rebuked Abimelech because of a well of water which Abimelech’s servants had seized.
NKJV.26: And Abimelech said, “I do not know who has done this thing; you did not tell me, nor had I heard of it until today.”
NKJV.27: So Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
NKJV.28: And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.
NKJV.29: Then Abimelech asked Abraham, “What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?”
NKJV.30: And he said, “You will take these seven ewe lambs from my hand, that they may be my witness that I have dug this well.”
NKJV.31: Therefore he called that place Beersheba, because the two of them swore an oath there.
NKJV.32: Thus they made a covenant at Beersheba. So Abimelech rose with Phichol, the commander of his army, and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
NKJV.33: Then Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
NKJV.34: And Abraham stayed in the land of the Philistines many days.

WEB.1: Yahweh visited Sarah as he had said, and Yahweh did to Sarah as he had spoken.
WEB.2: Sarah conceived, and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
WEB.3: Abraham called his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
WEB.4: Abraham circumcised his son, Isaac, when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
WEB.5: Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
WEB.6: Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. Everyone who hears will laugh with me.”
WEB.7: She said, “Who would have said to Abraham, that Sarah would nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”
WEB.8: The child grew, and was weaned. Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.
WEB.9: Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
WEB.10: Therefore she said to Abraham, “Cast out this servant and her son! For the son of this servant will not be heir with my son, Isaac.”
WEB.11: The thing was very grievous in Abraham’s sight on account of his son.
WEB.12: God said to Abraham, “Don’t let it be grievous in your sight because of the boy, and because of your servant. In all that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice. For your offspring  will be accounted as from Isaac.
WEB.13: I will also make a nation of the son of the servant, because he is your child .”
WEB.14: Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a bottle of water, and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder; and gave her the child, and sent her away. She departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
WEB.15: The water in the bottle was spent, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.
WEB.16: She went and sat down opposite him, a good way off, about a bow shot away. For she said, “Don’t let me see the death of the child.” She sat over against him, and lifted up her voice, and wept.
WEB.17: God heard the voice of the boy. The angel of God called to Hagar out of the sky, and said to her, “What ails you, Hagar? Don’t be afraid. For God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
WEB.18: Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him in your hand. For I will make him a great nation.”
WEB.19: God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went, filled the bottle with water, and gave the boy drink.
WEB.20: God was with the boy, and he grew. He lived in the wilderness, and became, as he grew up, an archer.
WEB.21: He lived in the wilderness of Paran. His mother took a wife for him out of the land of Egypt.
WEB.22: At that time, Abimelech and Phicol the captain of his army spoke to Abraham, saying, “God is with you in all that you do.
WEB.23: Now, therefore, swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son’s son. But according to the kindness that I have done to you, you shall do to me, and to the land in which you have lived as a foreigner.”
WEB.25: Abraham complained to Abimelech because of a water well, which Abimelech’s servants had violently taken away.
WEB.26: Abimelech said, “I don’t know who has done this thing. You didn’t tell me, and I didn’t hear of it until today.”
WEB.27: Abraham took sheep and cattle, and gave them to Abimelech. Those two made a covenant.
WEB.28: Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.
WEB.29: Abimelech said to Abraham, “What do these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves mean?”
WEB.30: He said, “You shall take these seven ewe lambs from my hand, that it may be a witness to me, that I have dug this well.”

CSB17.1: The LORD came to Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.2: Sarah became pregnant and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the appointed time God had told him. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.3: Abraham named his son who was born to him — the one Sarah bore to him — Isaac. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.4: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded him. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.5: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.6: Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears will laugh with me.” <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.7: She also said, “Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne a son for him <sup>[2]</sup> in his old age.”
CSB17.8: The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
CSB17.9: But Sarah saw the son mocking — the one Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.10: So she said to Abraham, “Drive out this slave with her son, for the son of this slave will not be a coheir with my son Isaac!” <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.11: This was very distressing to <sup>[3]</sup> Abraham because of his son.
CSB17.12: But God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed <sup>[4]</sup> about the boy and about your slave. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her, because your offspring will be traced through Isaac, <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.13: and I will also make a nation of the slave’s son <sup>ⓖ</sup> because he is your offspring.”
CSB17.14: Early in the morning Abraham got up, took bread and a waterskin, put them on Hagar’s shoulders, and sent her and the boy away. She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beer-sheba.
CSB17.15: When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes
CSB17.16: and went and sat at a distance, about a bowshot away, for she said, “I can’t bear to watch the boy die!” While she sat at a distance, she <sup>[5]</sup> wept loudly. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.17: God heard the boy crying, and the <sup>[6]</sup> angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, “What’s wrong, Hagar? Don’t be afraid, for God has heard the boy crying from the place where he is.
CSB17.18: Get up, help the boy up, and grasp his hand, for I will make him a great nation.”
CSB17.19: Then God opened her eyes, <sup>ⓘ</sup> and she saw a well. So she went and filled the waterskin and gave the boy a drink.
CSB17.20: God was with the boy, and he grew; he settled in the wilderness and became an archer.
CSB17.21: He settled in the Wilderness of Paran, and his mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
CSB17.22: At that time Abimelech, accompanied by Phicol the commander of his army, <sup>ⓙ</sup> said to Abraham, “God is with you in everything you do. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.23: Swear to me by God here and now, that you will not break an agreement with me or with my children and descendants. As I have been loyal to you, so you will be loyal to me and to the country where you are a resident alien.”
CSB17.25: But Abraham complained to Abimelech because of the well that Abimelech’s servants had seized. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.26: Abimelech replied, “I don’t know who did this thing. You didn’t report anything to me, so I hadn’t heard about it until today.”
CSB17.27: Abraham took flocks and herds and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.28: Abraham separated seven ewe lambs from the flock.
CSB17.29: And Abimelech said to Abraham, “Why have you separated these seven ewe lambs?”
CSB17.30: He replied, “You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from me so that this act <sup>[7]</sup> will serve as my witness that I dug this well.”
CSB17.31: Therefore that place was called Beer-sheba <sup>[8]</sup> <sup>ⓝ</sup> because it was there that the two of them swore an oath.
CSB17.32: After they had made a covenant at Beer-sheba, Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, left and returned to the land of the Philistines.
CSB17.33: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.34: And Abraham lived as an alien in the land of the Philistines for many days.

NLT.1: The LORD kept his word and did for Sarah exactly what he had promised.
NLT.2: She became pregnant, and she gave birth to a son for Abraham in his old age. This happened at just the time God had said it would.
NLT.3: And Abraham named their son Isaac.
NLT.4: Eight days after Isaac was born, Abraham circumcised him as God had commanded.
NLT.5: Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born.
NLT.6: And Sarah declared, “God has brought me laughter. All who hear about this will laugh with me.
NLT.7: Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse a baby? Yet I have given Abraham a son in his old age!”
NLT.8: When Isaac grew up and was about to be weaned, Abraham prepared a huge feast to celebrate the occasion.
NLT.9: But Sarah saw Ishmael — the son of Abraham and her Egyptian servant Hagar — making fun of her son, Isaac.
NLT.10: So she turned to Abraham and demanded, “Get rid of that slave woman and her son. He is not going to share the inheritance with my son, Isaac. I won’t have it!”
NLT.11: This upset Abraham very much because Ishmael was his son.
NLT.12: But God told Abraham, “Do not be upset over the boy and your servant. Do whatever Sarah tells you, for Isaac is the son through whom your descendants will be counted.
NLT.13: But I will also make a nation of the descendants of Hagar’s son because he is your son, too.”
NLT.14: So Abraham got up early the next morning, prepared food and a container of water, and strapped them on Hagar’s shoulders. Then he sent her away with their son, and she wandered aimlessly in the wilderness of Beersheba.
NLT.15: When the water was gone, she put the boy in the shade of a bush.
NLT.16: Then she went and sat down by herself about a hundred yards away. “I don’t want to watch the boy die,” she said, as she burst into tears.
NLT.17: But God heard the boy crying, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, “Hagar, what’s wrong? Do not be afraid! God has heard the boy crying as he lies there.
NLT.18: Go to him and comfort him, for I will make a great nation from his descendants.”
NLT.19: Then God opened Hagar’s eyes, and she saw a well full of water. She quickly filled her water container and gave the boy a drink.
NLT.20: And God was with the boy as he grew up in the wilderness. He became a skillful archer,
NLT.21: and he settled in the wilderness of Paran. His mother arranged for him to marry a woman from the land of Egypt.
NLT.22: About this time, Abimelech came with Phicol, his army commander, to visit Abraham. “God is obviously with you, helping you in everything you do,” Abimelech said.
NLT.23: “Swear to me in God’s name that you will never deceive me, my children, or any of my descendants. I have been loyal to you, so now swear that you will be loyal to me and to this country where you are living as a foreigner.”
NLT.24: Abraham replied, “Yes, I swear to it!”
NLT.25: Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well that Abimelech’s servants had taken by force from Abraham’s servants.
NLT.26: “This is the first I’ve heard of it,” Abimelech answered. “I have no idea who is responsible. You have never complained about this before.”
NLT.27: Abraham then gave some of his sheep, goats, and cattle to Abimelech, and they made a treaty.
NLT.28: But Abraham also took seven additional female lambs and set them off by themselves.
NLT.29: Abimelech asked, “Why have you set these seven apart from the others?”
NLT.30: Abraham replied, “Please accept these seven lambs to show your agreement that I dug this well.”
NLT.31: Then he named the place Beersheba (which means “well of the oath”), because that was where they had sworn the oath.
NLT.32: After making their covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech left with Phicol, the commander of his army, and they returned home to the land of the Philistines.
NLT.33: Then Abraham planted a tamarisk tree at Beersheba, and there he worshiped the LORD, the Eternal God.
NLT.34: And Abraham lived as a foreigner in Philistine country for a long time.

AMP.1: The LORD graciously remembered and visited Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for her as He had promised.
AMP.2: So Sarah conceived and gave birth to a son for Abraham in his old age, at the appointed time of which God had spoken to him.
AMP.3: Abraham named his son Isaac (laughter), the son to whom Sarah gave birth.
AMP.4: So Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, just as God had commanded him.
AMP.5: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born.
AMP.6: Sarah said, "God has made me laugh; all who hear [about our good news] will laugh with me."
AMP.7: And she said, "Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? For I have given birth to a son by him in his old age."
AMP.8: The child [Isaac] grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.
AMP.9: Now [as time went on] Sarah saw [Ishmael] the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking [Isaac].
AMP.10: Therefore she said to Abraham, "Drive out this maid and her son, for the son of this maid shall not be an heir with my son Isaac."
AMP.11: The situation distressed Abraham greatly because of his son [Ishmael].
AMP.12: God said to Abraham, "Do not let it distress you because of Ishmael and your maid; whatever Sarah tells you, listen to her and do what she asks, for your descendants will be named through Isaac.
AMP.13: And I will also make a nation of [Ishmael] the son of the maid, because he is your descendant."
AMP.14: So Abraham got up early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water and gave them to Hagar, putting them on her shoulder, and gave her the boy, and sent her away. And she left [but lost her way] and wandered [aimlessly] in the Wilderness of Beersheba.
AMP.15: When the water in the skin was all gone, Hagar abandoned the boy under one of the bushes.
AMP.16: Then she went and sat down opposite him, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Do not let me see the boy die." And as she sat down opposite him, she raised her voice and wept.
AMP.17: God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy from where he is [resting].
AMP.18: Get up, help the boy up, and hold him by the hand, for I will make him a great nation."
AMP.19: Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water; and she went and filled the [empty] skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
AMP.20: God was with Ishmael, and he grew and developed; and he lived in the wilderness and became an [expert] archer.
AMP.21: He lived in the wilderness of Paran; and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
AMP.22: Now at that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do;
AMP.23: so now, swear to me here by God that you will not deal unfairly with me [by breaking any agreements we have] or with my son or with my descendants, but as I have treated you with kindness, you shall do the same to me and to the land in which you have sojourned (temporarily lived)."
AMP.25: Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water which the servants of Abimelech had [violently] seized [from him],
AMP.26: Abimelech said, "I do not know who did this thing. Indeed, you did not tell me, and I did not hear of it until today."
AMP.27: So Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant (binding agreement).
AMP.28: Then Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs of the flock,
AMP.29: and Abimelech said to Abraham, "What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set apart?"
AMP.30: Abraham said, "You are to accept these seven ewe lambs from me as a witness for me, that I dug this well."
AMP.31: Therefore that place was called Beersheba (Well of the Oath or Well of the Seven), because there the two of them swore an oath.
AMP.32: So they made a covenant at Beersheba; then Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
AMP.33: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree at Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD [in prayer], the Eternal God.
AMP.34: And Abraham lived [as a resident alien] in the land of the Philistines for many days.

NET.25: But Abraham lodged a complaint against Abimelech concerning a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized.
NET.26: “I do not know who has done this thing,” Abimelech replied. “Moreover, you did not tell me. I did not hear about it until today.”
NET.27: Abraham took some sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech. The two of them made a treaty.
NET.28: Then Abraham set seven ewe lambs apart from the flock by themselves.
NET.29: Abimelech asked Abraham, “What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs that you have set apart?”
NET.30: He replied, “You must take these seven ewe lambs from my hand as legal proof that I dug this well.”
NET.31: That is why he named that place Beer Sheba, because the two of them swore an oath there.
NET.32: So they made a treaty at Beer Sheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, returned to the land of the Philistines.
NET.33: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer Sheba. There he worshiped the LORD, the eternal God.
NET.34: So Abraham stayed in the land of the Philistines for quite some time.
